_readme: Historical startup ideas with known outcomes, used by tests/eval/run.eval.ts
to measure whether validate-idea's judgment is any good.
Each idea is written as it would have been PITCHED AT THE TIME -- present
tense, no hindsight, no outcome words. An entry that leaks its own answer
('the company that went on to...') measures nothing.
contamination: how likely a frontier model is to recognise the specific
company from the description alone. The famous cases are unavoidably
'high' -- a model that recognises Airbnb is scoring its memory of the
outcome, not the idea. The harness therefore reports every number twice:
once over the whole set, once over the low+medium subset only. The second
number is the honest one. See docs/eval/calibration-report.md.
actualOutcome 'unknown' = genuinely contested, counted in NEITHER
numerator nor denominator. Kept in the set because the interesting output
for these is the reasoning, not the score.

ideas.idea: A website where people rent out an air mattress in their spare room to strangers attending a nearby conference. Hosts set their own price; we take a cut of each booking.
ideas.note: Canonical false negative. Sounds unsafe and tiny. A naive skeptic kills it.

ideas.idea: A folder on your computer that automatically syncs to the cloud and to your other computers. No manual upload step.
ideas.note: Canonical false negative. 'You can do this with rsync and an FTP account' was the actual top comment.

ideas.idea: Seven lines of code that let a developer accept credit card payments without talking to a bank, filling in a merchant application, or waiting two weeks for approval.
ideas.note: Entering a market with entrenched incumbents and a regulatory moat. Wedge is developer experience.

ideas.idea: A website where you watch other people play video games, live, and chat with them while they do it.
ideas.note: Sounds like a hobby, not a market. Tests whether the model can price an audience it doesn't belong to.

ideas.idea: A chat app for work teams, organised into channels. Replaces internal email. Free tier, paid per seat above a message-history limit.
ideas.note: IRC, HipChat, Campfire already exist. Tests 'crowded market' reflex.

ideas.idea: A professional design tool that runs entirely in a browser tab, with multiple designers editing the same file at the same time.
ideas.note: Attacking a dominant desktop incumbent on a technically hard axis.

ideas.idea: Drag-and-drop design software for people who are not designers, with thousands of pre-made templates for social posts and presentations.
ideas.note: Non-consumption wedge. Competitors serve professionals; this serves everyone else.

ideas.idea: A hosted storefront so anyone can sell products online without a developer. Monthly subscription plus payment fees.
ideas.note: Marketplaces already own the demand side. Tests whether 'own your own store' reads as a real wedge.

ideas.idea: Video meetings that just work — one click to join, no plugin, no account required for guests, free for calls under forty minutes.
ideas.note: Extremely crowded, incumbents were free and bundled. Won on reliability alone.

ideas.idea: A platform that lets a writer charge readers a monthly fee for an email newsletter. We handle payments and hosting and take a percentage.
ideas.note: 'Email is a solved problem' reflex. The wedge is payments, not email.

ideas.idea: Always-on voice chat rooms for groups of friends playing games together, with persistent text channels alongside.
ideas.note: Incumbent voice software was widely hated but entrenched and free.

ideas.idea: A single app that is a notes app, a wiki, a task board and a database, where users assemble their own tools from blocks.
ideas.note: 'Does everything, therefore nothing' is a legitimate criticism that happened to be wrong here.

ideas.idea: A four-hundred-dollar countertop press that squeezes juice from proprietary single-serve produce packs sold by subscription. The press connects to wifi to verify each pack is fresh.
ideas.note: The packs can be squeezed by hand. Hardware adds no value over the consumable.

ideas.idea: A subscription streaming service showing premium scripted shows in ten-minute episodes, designed to be watched only on a phone during commutes.
ideas.note: Nearly two billion raised. Tests whether funding is mistaken for validation.

ideas.idea: A self-balancing two-wheeled electric transporter that people stand on. We expect cities to redesign around it.
ideas.note: Real technology, real hype, no adoption. Failure is behavioural, not technical.

ideas.idea: Consumer eyeglasses with a built-in camera and heads-up display, worn all day in public.
ideas.note: Social rejection, not capability. Tests whether the model weighs social risk at all.

ideas.idea: Online grocery delivery across the country, with our own automated warehouses and delivery fleet, built out ahead of demand.
ideas.note: The idea was right and the timing and capital structure were fatal. Tests timing sensitivity.

ideas.idea: An online store for pet supplies, shipping heavy low-margin goods like litter and dog food nationwide, with heavy brand advertising to build awareness fast.
ideas.note: Unit economics negative per order at every volume.

ideas.idea: A photo sharing app with no privacy settings at all — every photo you take is visible to anyone physically near you.
ideas.note: Forty-one million raised pre-launch. The premise is the defect.

ideas.idea: A social network exclusively for dogs, where owners create a profile for each pet and the pets follow each other.
ideas.note: Generic dud. Should be an easy kill; if the model scores this above 40 the whole set is suspect.

ideas.idea: A blockchain-based loyalty points system for independent coffee shops, so customers can earn points at one cafe and spend them at another.
ideas.note: Technology in search of a problem; a shared spreadsheet solves it. Easy kill.

ideas.idea: A smart refrigerator with interior cameras that recognises what you are running low on and automatically reorders it from a grocery partner.
ideas.note: Repeatedly attempted, never adopted. Hardware cost vs. a thirty-second task.

ideas.idea: A microblogging platform identical to the dominant one but with better moderation and no advertising, funded by user donations.
ideas.note: No distribution wedge against a network effect. Easy kill.

ideas.idea: An on-demand service that sends a valet to park your car anywhere in the city for a flat fee, cheaper than a parking garage.
ideas.note: Labour cost per transaction exceeds price. Several funded attempts, all dead.

ideas.idea: Accounting software for very small businesses, sold as a low monthly subscription in the browser instead of a several-hundred-dollar desktop licence, with bank feeds imported automatically.
ideas.note: Several independent winners. Business-model wedge against an entrenched desktop incumbent.

ideas.idea: A tool that queues social media posts across a person's accounts and publishes them on a schedule, free for a few posts a week and a monthly fee above that.
ideas.note: Boring, obviously copyable, no moat on paper. Multiple durable businesses exist anyway.

ideas.idea: A password manager that stores encrypted credentials, generates strong passwords and fills them in automatically, sold per family per year.
ideas.note: Browsers give a version away free. Tests whether 'the platform bundles this' is treated as automatically fatal.

ideas.idea: An app that collects your laundry from your door, washes it, and returns it the next day for a flat fee per bag, in one city to start.
ideas.note: Many funded attempts, near-total mortality. Logistics cost per order exceeds willingness to pay.

ideas.idea: A hyperlocal news site covering a single neighbourhood, written by one reporter, funded by advertising from businesses on that street.
ideas.note: Audience ceiling is smaller than the cost of one salary. Repeatedly attempted.

ideas.idea: A mobile app that pays users a few cents in credit for each advertisement they watch, monetised by charging advertisers more than we pay out.
ideas.note: Attracts exactly the users advertisers value least. Adversarial-selection dud, should be an easy kill.

ideas.idea: An invite-only audio-only social app where anyone can drop into a live room and listen to or join a conversation. No recording, nothing persists.
ideas.note: Explosive growth then near-total collapse. Any single label is a lie; excluded from scoring.

ideas.idea: A two-thousand-dollar stationary exercise bike with a screen, sold with a monthly subscription to live instructor-led classes.
ideas.note: Enormous success followed by a severe correction. Genuinely contested.

ideas.idea: A meal-kit subscription that ships pre-portioned ingredients and recipe cards weekly, so people cook at home without planning or shopping.
ideas.note: Category is real and large; nearly every individual entrant struggled on retention and CAC.

ideas.idea: A browser extension that reads the page you are on and answers questions about it using a language model, free with a paid tier for heavy users.
ideas.note: Contemporary, unresolved. Included as a live control: this one the founder can resolve later with a real Prediction.
